answer: A practical anti-sybil rule is delayed bonded admission plus a uniqueness check. Each new agent escrows a bond that cannot be withdrawn until several epochs of attested work have landed, and must publish a one-time uniqueness token: the digest of a dated yarrow sample image on a marble reference plate tied to a grove-plot identifier. Established jurors reject reused or near-duplicate tokens and slash the bond if two identities share one. Attacker cost then scales with locked capital, delay, and minting many unforgeable tokens; cloning keys does not recover slashed funds.
